name: Region Capture and Element Capture
plain: Crops a screen capture to part of the page, no prompt.
meaning: Lets an app crop a tab capture to one element and hide the rest, so a recording shows only that element. Cannot reach beyond the tab capture the person already allowed.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt of its own; it needs an existing tab capture stream.
steps: Capture the current tab with getDisplayMedia
Create a CropTarget or RestrictionTarget from an element

limits.headline: Can crop a screen share to one part of the page, with no extra prompt
limits.user_action: You are already sharing the tab, then the app limits the view to one panel
can: Crop your shared tab to show only one box or element
Hide the rest of the page from the recording or call
Change which part is shown while you keep sharing
cannot: Start any capture on its own; you must already be sharing the tab
Show anything beyond the tab you chose to share
Capture other tabs, windows or your screen
Work in Firefox, Safari or any phone browser
limits.reach_label: A piece of one shared tab
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app crop a tab share to one part of the page, with no extra prompt.

marketing.name: Region Capture
marketing.pitch: Chrome explains that apps can crop a tab capture to a single element so a recording shows only that part.

story.for_you: You do not see a new prompt. After you already agreed to share a tab, the app may show just one box, such as a slide, instead of the whole page. It can also hide a sidebar or chat that you did not want in a recording.
story.for_makers: Makers get cleaner recordings and shared views without asking people to crop things by hand. A call app can send only the slide, or a streaming tool can cut out the app around a canvas. It cannot reach past what the person already shared.

use_cases.example: In a web call you share a tab with slides, and the call shows only the slide, not the browser tabs or notes next to it.
A design review tool records just the canvas, so the video does not show the comment panel or your other tabs.
A browser game tool records the game canvas only, and leaves out your chat panel when you stream a match.
A web classroom records the whiteboard area and leaves out private student names in the side list.
A live event page crops the shared tab to the video player, so a viewer sees the show with no page chrome.
A bug report tool captures only the broken widget on the page and ignores the user's private account details nearby.

risks: Only hides what an app agrees to hide
Hidden parts may still be in the page

technical_bounds: Not for window or screen capture
